sections.h2: What a Lebanon seller needs to know first
sections.html:
Lebanon packs about 26,479 people into 4.17 square miles of older homes, many of them rented, with a typical owner's home valued at $156,500. At that price level, repairs, taxes and closing costs take a large share of any sale.

The city is Lebanon County's seat, 26 miles east of Harrisburg and 88 miles northwest of Philadelphia. Most homes here are rented, so landlords make up a big part of both the selling and the buying side. A seller of a tenant-occupied property should expect investors to ask for the rent roll, the rental license and the last inspection results. With rent near $992 against a $156,500 home value, the rental market is a major buyer of Lebanon houses.

A Lebanon owner can use a broker, post the sign personally or take a cash bid for the house. In every case the deed is filed at the courthouse on South 8th Street, and the county treasurer keeps the tax payment records.

sections.h2: City of Lebanon rental license rules
sections.html:
Every dwelling unit or rooming unit offered for rent in the city must have a rental license, and each parcel with rental units needs its own application. A buyer inherits the license history, so it pays to have your file in order.

  • A $25 penalty is added every 60 days a fee stays unpaid after billing.
  • Renewal is delayed or denied if money is owed to the city or code violations are open.
  • The owner must keep a contract with a trash hauler on file, and a property manager must be within 20 miles of the city limit.
  • Grass and weeds cannot exceed 12 inches, snow and ice must come off sidewalks within 24 hours after a snowfall ends, and inoperable or unlicensed vehicles cannot sit on a premises more than 5 days.
  • Smoke alarms and carbon monoxide detectors are required, and a license revoked for unsafe conditions costs $100 to reinstate.

Questions go to the city's code enforcement office at 717-639-2800, option 2, at 735 Cumberland Street. For a rental, put copies of the current license and any violation notice in your file before you answer a buyer.

The city's Building and Zoning Division, part of Public Works, runs permits and zoning. A zoning permit is required for building or altering a structure, adding an addition, demolishing or moving one, and putting up fences, decks, sheds and garages. It is also required for a change of use, a swimming pool or hot tub deeper than 18 inches, and a sign.

Construction inspections are done by outside code inspection firms under contract, and the city asks for at least 24 hours' notice. A deck or shed that an earlier owner added without a permit is something an inspector may catch. Settle that question before listing, or ask the zoning office what the city would require.

The city zoning ordinance defines 10 districts. A Zoning Hearing Board hears variance and special exception requests.

sections.h2: How do county taxes and the Tax Claim Bureau affect a sale?
sections.html:
The Lebanon County Treasurer collects the county real estate tax, the city tax and now the Lebanon City School District bill, so one office can tell you whether anything is owed on a city parcel. The Tax Claim Bureau charges $15 per parcel for a tax certification, and a mailed request must include a stamped return envelope.

Delinquent taxes pass to the Tax Claim Bureau each January. The owner is sent a certified letter showing the balance, interest and costs, along with the date to pay in order to avoid a sale. About 17 months after that first notice the bureau mails a notice of sale. Buyers at the upset sale take the property subject to judgments, liens and mortgages, and bidders must pre-register for a $25 fee.

If you are behind on taxes, pay or arrange the balance before closing. Once a property is on the sale list, the process follows a fixed bureau and court calendar.

sections.h2: Assessment appeals and recording the deed
sections.html:
Assessment appeals are due each September 1 by 4:30 at the Board of Assessment Revision. A notice that arrives late waits for the following year. The filing fee for a residential property of one to four units is $50 and is not refunded. You or an authorized representative must attend the hearing, and the board can raise, lower or keep the assessment.

Filings go to the Assessment Office at 400 South 8th Street, Room 118. Owners can also view their records free on DataScout, using the control number and web password printed on the tax bill.

The Recorder of Deeds is in Room 107 of the same courthouse, open on weekdays, and accepts cash or check only. Most documents come back the following business day, and the Assessment Office must certify the parcel identifier before a deed records. The state transfer tax is 1 percent, and the recorder's office adds any local share when it collects.

sections.h2: Steps for a Lebanon sale, start to finish
sections.html:
The order below keeps a sale from stalling at the courthouse.

  1. Call the treasurer's office to find out whether any county, city or school tax is owed on the parcel.
  2. If you rent the house out, gather the current rental license, any violation notice and the last inspection results.
  3. Ask the zoning office about any deck, shed, fence or addition built without a permit.
  4. Request a $15 tax certification from the Tax Claim Bureau if the title company asks for one, and include a stamped return envelope with a mailed request.
  5. Bring the deed to Room 107 of the courthouse on South 8th Street with cash or a check, after the Assessment Office certifies the parcel identifier.

A cash buyer skips the lender appraisal, but every step above still applies. Ask who handles each one before you sign.

sections.h2: Which Lebanon houses suit a cash offer?
sections.html:
A cash sale suits a house with heavy repairs, a rental carrying open code items, a vacant building or an estate. It is also useful when tax delinquency puts the house on a calendar you cannot move.

Price comparison matters here because the median value is modest. Add up the commission, repairs, transfer tax and months of ownership on a listing, and compare that net with a cash figure. To ask for an offer on a Lebanon house in its present state, contact Cash Home Buyers.

faqs.q: Does Lebanon require a rental license?
faqs.a: Yes. Every dwelling unit or rooming unit offered for rent in the City of Lebanon must have a license, with a separate application for each parcel that has rental units.

faqs.q: When are Lebanon County assessment appeals due?
faqs.a: September 1 each year, filed with the Board of Assessment Revision at the Assessment Office on South 8th Street. A residential appeal costs $50.

faqs.q: How long can Lebanon County delinquent taxes sit before a sale?
faqs.a: Unpaid taxes move to the Tax Claim Bureau every January, and owners have until the last working day of the next June. A notice of sale follows about 17 months after the first notice.

faqs.q: Where is a Lebanon deed recorded?
faqs.a: At the Lebanon County Recorder of Deeds, Room 107 of the courthouse at 400 South 8th Street. The office takes cash or check and can also accept electronic recording.

faqs.q: Which school district serves the City of Lebanon?
faqs.a: The Lebanon School District, which covers the city and West Lebanon Township. The county treasurer now collects its tax bill for city parcels.
